chunks: And ʿAmr ibn Shimr narrated from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
When Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down:
Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, stone altars, and divining arrows are filth from the work of Satan, so avoid it.

It was said: O Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, what is gambling? He said: Everything by which gambling is done, even dice and walnuts. It was said: Then what are the stone altars? He said: What they slaughtered for their gods. It was said: Then what are the divining arrows? He said: Their arrows by which they sought division.

key_terms.الْأَزْلَامُ: divining arrows used to seek decisions or allotments
key_terms.الْأَنْصَابُ: objects or places associated with sacrificial offerings to false gods
key_terms.تُقُومِرَ: to be used for gambling or wagering
key_terms.رِجْسٌ: filth and impurity in a moral and religious sense
key_terms.قِدَاحُهُمُ: their arrows or lots used in divinatory practice

ai.seo_question: What do maysir, ansab, and azlam mean in Qur'an 5:90?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the meanings of terms in the Qur'anic prohibition of intoxicants and gambling-related practices. It identifies maysir as all forms of gambling, ansab as what was sacrificed for idols, and azlam as the arrows used for divination and seeking decisions.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3587 - It is narrated from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said:
"When Allah (swt), the Blessed and Exalted, revealed the verse: 'Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone alters [to other than Allah (swt)], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid them' (Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:90).
The people asked: 'O Messenger of Allah (swt), what is gambling (maysir)?'
He (sw) replied: 'Everything that involves betting, even dice and walnuts.'
They asked: 'What are the stone alters (ansab)?'
He (sw) said: 'They are the sacrifices offered to their idols.'
They asked: 'What are the divining arrows (azlam)?'
He (sw) said: 'They are their arrows used for seeking decisions or division.'"
